text:
sofia: FYI we pushed the tiered-prefix-cache + NVMe spillover canary this morning. Short summary: p50 -13%, p95 -24%, estimated infra token cost down ~31% on convo-heavy samples. :tada:

ben: Nice. What does NVMe spillover mean here?

sofia: When RAM prefix cache is full we now spill cold prefixes to local NVMe with async read-ahead. Hot prefixes stay in RAM and we use an LRU+freq hybrid to promote items. The idea is to keep warm KV reads fast and avoid OOM/massive full-prefix reads.

rachel: Canary size and workload?

deploy-bot: Canary report (nvme-prefix-2027-07-12): 140k requests, 65/35 chat/completion split, median seq 48, p50 41ms -> 36ms, p95 220ms -> 167ms, error rate stable 0.03% -> 0.03%. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/perf/nvme-prefix-2027-07-12

tom: Any regressions or host impacts?

sofia: We saw ~9% extra IO on NVMe under synthetic churn, but CPU and memory stayed within headroom. Added a throttle (nvme_io_qps) and fallback to full-prefix reads if NVMe latency spikes. No customer-facing regressions in canary.

ben: Config snippet?

sofia: Paste of the conservative canary config:

```
prefix_cache:
  ram_capacity_mb: 5120
  policy: lru_freq_hybrid
  promotion_threshold: 3
nvme_spillover:
  enabled: true
  device: /dev/nvme0n1
  max_qps: 1200
  read_ahead_ms: 20
  promote_on_read_hits: true
async_prefetch:
  enabled: true
  max_workers: 12
  backoff_ms: 50
```

rachel: Rollout plan?

sofia: Canary -> 3% -> 20% (8h) -> 80% (24h) -> 100% (48h). Auto-rollback if p95 increases >5% or error rate delta >0.15% or NVMe error rate >0.02%. Monitoring hooks added.

cost-bot: If effect holds across fleet, projected monthly infra token spend reduction ~28-33% for conversation tiers. Logged under COST-2027-07-NVME.

tom: Please add a short note to model-onboarding that NVMe spillover may affect cache hit heatmaps and cost attribution. Also add the new thresholds to the runbook.

sofia: Will do. I'll draft a 1-slide summary for all-hands and post the canary dash + config in #docs. Closing thread  will update after 20% step or if any alerts fire.
